books.title: The Pilgrim's Progress
books.author: John Bunyan
books.blurb: A man named Christian, a burden on his back and a book in his hand, flees the City of Destruction for the Celestial City. The road runs through the Slough of Despond, Vanity Fair, the Valley of the Shadow of Death and the dungeons of Doubting Castle. Part Two follows his wife Christiana and their children along the same road — the most widely read allegory in the English language. This edition carries one hundred and four wood-engravings by Charles Bennett, cut on wood by Joseph Swain for the New York printing of 1860, set where that printing set them.
books.source: The Works of John Bunyan, ed. George Offor, 1855, via Project Gutenberg and Standard Ebooks; illustrations from Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, D. Appleton and Company, New York, 1860, drawn by Charles Bennett and engraved by Joseph Swain

books.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
books.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
books.blurb: The twelve stories that made Sherlock Holmes, as they ran in the Strand Magazine between 1891 and 1892 — a king’s photograph, a pawnbroker paid to copy out an encyclopaedia, a stepfather who is not what he seems, and a whistle in the night at Stoke Moran. Set from the Harper & Brothers printing of 1892, with Sidney Paget’s plates and a colour plate at the head of every Adventure. This is a proofing copy — corrections welcome.
books.source: Harper & Brothers, New York, 1892 — collated from two scans of two copies of that printing, read independently
books.license: Text and Sidney Paget’s plates public domain; cover, Adventure plates and editorial matter © RFRMD Word Labs LLC

books.title: The Mortification of Sin in Believers
books.author: John Owen
books.blurb: Owen preaching to Oxford undergraduates in 1656 on eight words of Paul: if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live. The most searching book in English on how sin is actually killed, and on the several ways a man deceives himself that it has been. Set from the 1668 printing. This is a proofing copy — corrections welcome.
books.source: EEBO-TCP A53715 (Wing O787), the 1668 printing, keyed and released CC0
books.license: Text public domain; editorial matter © RFRMD Word Labs LLC

books.title: The Rare Jewel of Christian Contentment
books.author: Jeremiah Burroughs
books.blurb: Sermons on Paul’s "I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content" — learned, Burroughs insists, and therefore teachable. He takes contentment apart: what it is, what it is not, the excellence of it, and the many ways a discontented heart argues with God. Set from the 1649 printing. This is a proofing copy — corrections welcome.
books.source: EEBO-TCP A30598 (Wing B6103), the 1649 printing, keyed and released CC0
books.license: Text public domain; editorial matter © RFRMD Word Labs LLC

books.title: Meditations and Discourses on the Glory of Christ
books.author: John Owen
books.blurb: Owen’s last work, in two parts: the glory of Christ in his person, office and grace, and then the same meditations applied to the unconverted and to saints under spiritual decay. Set from two independently keyed copies of the London printing of 1691, collated against each other — neither copy is the whole book. Spelling and capitalisation modernised; Scripture left exactly as printed. This is a proofing copy — corrections welcome.

books.title: The Sovereignty of God
books.author: A. W. Pink
books.blurb: Pink sets out what Scripture says of God’s rule — in creation, in salvation, in reprobation, and over the human will — and then answers the objections plainly, one at a time. Set from the 1918 first edition, Bible Truth Depot, Swengel, and carrying all three appendices that the abridged later edition leaves out. This is a proofing copy — corrections welcome.

books.title: Tales of the Covenanters
books.author: Robert Pollok
books.blurb: Three tales from the years of persecution in Scotland, when soldiers hunted the Presbyterians who would not renounce their covenant. Helen of the Glen, Ralph Gemmell and The Persecuted Family follow ordinary households — children, shepherds, mothers — caught between the dragoons and their consciences.
books.source: Internet Archive scan of the 1895 Oliphant Anderson & Ferrier edition

books.title: Tales of the Covenanters
books.author: Ellen Jane Guthrie
books.blurb: The covenanting martyrs told as a series of short tales, each tied to the place that remembers it: Bothwell Bridge, Peden's Stone, the murder at Inchdarnie — and the persecutors, Culzean and the Laird of Lag, whose names the hunted did not forget.

books.title: Treasure Island
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.blurb: An old seaman dies at the Admiral Benbow with a map in his sea-chest, and Jim Hawkins ships aboard the Hispaniola to find what it marks. So does a one-legged cook named Long John Silver — the most companionable villain in English fiction — and half the crew are his.

books.title: The Swiss Family Robinson
books.author: Johann David Wyss
books.blurb: A father, a mother and their four sons — Fritz, Ernest, Jack and Franz — are wrecked on an island when the crew abandons ship. What follows is a family building a world: salvaging the wreck, taming the land, making a home in a tree, and turning every difficulty into a lesson.

books.title: The Mystery at Dark Cedars
books.author: Edith Lavell
books.blurb: Money is vanishing from a miserly old woman's shuttered house, and her orphaned niece is blamed for it. Mary Louise Gay — sixteen, and a detective by vocation — decides the obvious suspect is the wrong one, and sets out to prove it.
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: The Mystery of the Fires
books.author: Edith Lavell
books.blurb: A month at Shady Nook with her chum Jane, and Mary Louise Gay means to do nothing but swim and canoe. Then a bungalow burns, and another, and the little summer colony begins eyeing its neighbours. The girl detective is on holiday; the fires are not.
books.source: Project Gutenberg ebook 43583, retrieved via OpenChapter.io
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: The Mystery of the Secret Band
books.author: Edith Lavell
books.blurb: Christmas is coming, and Mary Louise Gay is handed her first real assignment — two weeks of work away from home, and her father's trade at last. Then the robberies begin: a midnight visitor, an abandoned house, a blow in the dark, and a band nobody can name.
books.source: Project Gutenberg ebook 43584, retrieved via OpenChapter.io
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: The Sugar Creek Gang Goes North
books.author: Paul Hutchens
books.blurb: The gang heads north for a camping trip, hoping to see their friend Snow-in-the-face again. What they find instead is a kidnapping — and Bill Collins and the rest set about solving it between the tents and the timber.
books.source: Project Gutenberg ebook 56554, retrieved via OpenChapter.io
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: The Sugar Creek Gang Digs for Treasure
books.author: Paul Hutchens
books.blurb: Camping in the north woods, Bill Collins and Little Jim turn the shore into Robinson Crusoe's island and go hunting imaginary treasure. Then the game stops being a game: there is a kidnapper, a ransom, and money nobody can find.
books.source: Project Gutenberg ebook 56553, retrieved via OpenChapter.io
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

books.title: The Green Tent Mystery at Sugar Creek
books.author: Paul Hutchens
books.blurb: Three boys walking home past an abandoned cemetery on the darkest night of the summer see a light out among the stones, and somebody digging. What the Sugar Creek Gang turns up keeps them busy until autumn.
books.license: Text public domain in the United States

note: Every edition begins with a work long out of copyright, usually an original printing we can name. We set the text properly — collating the copies that survive, and clearing away what scanning and re-keying leave behind — so the book reads well on the page and sounds right read aloud. Where we mark a division inside a chapter, it is one the author announces himself. Every edition says on its own front matter what was done to its text. They are free to read and free to keep; our hope is that they reach people, grow their love for the Lord, and increase their joy in reading.
